records.text: The Obama administration sent one or two Boeing 757s loaded with hundreds of millions of dollars in cash to Iran, leaving banks in Virginia, Maryland, and Washington, D.C. without money.
records.speaker: Donald J. Trump

appearances.snippet: They were, if we didn't do the attack or if I'll go a step further, if I didn't terminate the Iran nuclear deal given to us, one of the worst deals ever made by Barack Hussein Obama. Remember when they sent Boeing 757s over there loaded with cash. ... Hundreds of millions of dollars. You would have been very happy. This was a wonderful. They said hundreds of millions. People forget that. Does anybody remember? ... Right. You remember hundreds of millions of dollars in a Boeing 757. I think that two of them loaded. They took the seats out. ... And they put cash. And it was so much that there wasn't a bank in Virginia, Maryland or D.C. that had any money left. ... They stripped them of all their money, put it into planes, sent it to Iran almost as ransom.

verification.notes: The official transcript confirms Trump made the statement. The Obama administration did transfer 00 million in foreign cash to Iran as the first installment of a .7 billion settlement, but authoritative records do not support the specific Boeing 757 count, seats-removed story, or claim that regional banks were stripped of all money.

records.text: Under Barack Obama, the United States armed Al-Qaeda offshoots while helping Israel turn Syria into a failed state.
records.speaker: Ana Kasparian

appearances.snippet: And a lot of people don't know this. We wanted to assist Israel in turning. Syria into a failed state and we certainly succeeded in that mission so under Obama we started arming literal terrorists including like Al-Qaeda offshoots

verification.notes: The Obama administration ran covert and overt programs arming vetted Syrian rebels, and official reporting confirms some U.S.-supplied equipment was surrendered to or captured by al-Nusra, an al-Qaeda affiliate. Evidence does not show a stated U.S. policy to arm al-Qaeda directly, nor does it establish that the program purpose was to help Israel turn Syria into a failed state.
